tools.name: run_report

property_id.description: GA4 property ID. Accepts: bare number (12345), string ("12345"), or resource name ("properties/12345")

date_ranges.description: Date ranges for the report. Each object has: start_date (required, YYYY-MM-DD or relative: "today", "yesterday", "NdaysAgo"), end_date (required, same format), name (optional). Example: [{"start_date": "30daysAgo", "end_date": "today"}]

dimensions.description: List of dimension names. See: https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/api-schema#dimensions Example: ["country", "city"]

metrics.description: List of metric names. See: https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/api-schema#metrics Example: ["activeUsers", "sessions"]

dimension_filter.description: Optional dimension filter expression. Supports: simple filter (string_filter, numeric_filter, in_list_filter, between_filter), not_expression, and_group, or_group. Example: {"filter": {"field_name": "country", "string_filter": {"match_type": "EXACT", "value": "US"}}}

metric_filter.description: Optional metric filter expression. Same structure as dimension_filter. Example: {"filter": {"field_name": "activeUsers", "numeric_filter": {"operation": "GREATER_THAN", "value": {"int64_value": 100}}}}

order_bys.description: Optional ordering. List of order_by objects. Each can have: dimension (with dimension_name and optional order_type: ALPHANUMERIC, CASE_INSENSITIVE_ALPHANUMERIC, NUMERIC), metric (with metric_name), or pivot; plus desc (bool). Example: [{"metric": {"metric_name": "activeUsers"}, "desc": true}]

limit.description: Maximum rows to return (max 250000). Used for pagination.

return_property_quota.description: Whether to include property quota information in the response.

tools.behavior: Builds dateRanges, dimensions and metrics; names are wrapped as {name}. Recursively converts snake_case keys of date ranges, filters and ordering to camelCase. Optional limit/offset are sent as decimal strings, with currencyCode and returnPropertyQuota when supplied. POST runReport and return JSON. Property operations route through the cached Google account, or probe configured clients on cache miss; cached HTTP 403 clears the entry. API errors become MCP tool-error content.
notes: property_id is a JSON string despite description claiming acceptance of a bare number; there is no coercion annotation.
Filter, order and range structures use arbitrary serde_json::Value; documented nested shapes and numeric limits are not schema constraints. No local validation of GA field names or row limits.

tools.name: login
tools.description: Re-authenticate a configured Google account via interactive OAuth. Starts a local loopback listener, opens Google's consent screen in the default browser, captures the callback, and writes a new refresh_token to the account's credentials file. Use when an existing refresh_token has been revoked or expired. The MCP server must be restarted after success for the new token to take effect. Requires an OAuth Desktop-app client_id/client_secret, either in the [[accounts]] entry in config.toml or already present in the existing credentials file.

name.description: The account name from config.toml ([[accounts]] `name` field) to re-authenticate. Starts a loopback OAuth flow, opens the consent URL in the default browser, captures the callback, and writes a new refresh_token to that account's credentials file.

tools.behavior: Loads the named account from config.toml, resolves Desktop OAuth client credentials, binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port, opens Google consent for analytics.edit and analytics.readonly, waits up to 300 seconds for a callback, checks state, exchanges the code and overwrites that account credentials JSON. Existing in-memory clients require restart.
notes: Always registered, but requires a config.toml account; ADC-only startup provides no configured account for this tool. Startup loads credential files first, so this tool cannot bootstrap a server with missing credentials.

tools.name: run_realtime_report
tools.description:
Run a realtime report on a GA4 property. Returns data for the last 30 minutes by default (configurable via minute_ranges).

## References
- Realtime dimensions: https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/realtime-api-schema#dimensions
- Realtime metrics: https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/realtime-api-schema#metrics

No date_ranges parameter — use minute_ranges to control the time window.
Only user-scoped custom dimensions (customUser:*) are supported; custom metrics are not.

Filters and ordering use the same format as run_report.

property_id.description: GA4 property ID. Accepts: bare number (12345), string ("12345"), or resource name ("properties/12345")

dimensions.description: List of realtime dimension names. See: https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/realtime-api-schema#dimensions Example: ["country", "unifiedScreenName"]

metrics.description: List of realtime metric names. See: https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/realtime-api-schema#metrics Example: ["activeUsers"]

dimension_filter.description: Optional dimension filter expression. Same structure as run_report's dimension_filter.

metric_filter.description: Optional metric filter expression. Same structure as run_report's metric_filter.

order_bys.description: Optional ordering. Same structure as run_report's order_bys.

minute_ranges.description: Optional minute ranges for the realtime report. By default covers the last 30 minutes. Each object has: start_minutes_ago (int, max 29), end_minutes_ago (int, min 0), name (optional). Example: [{"start_minutes_ago": 10, "end_minutes_ago": 0}]

return_property_quota.description: Whether to include property quota information in the response.

tools.behavior: Builds named dimensions/metrics and shared filter/order/quota/limit/offset fields as for run_report; recursively converts minute_ranges to camelCase and POSTs runRealtimeReport. Property operations route through the cached Google account, or probe configured clients on cache miss; cached HTTP 403 clears the entry. API errors become MCP tool-error content.
notes: property_id is a JSON string despite description claiming acceptance of a bare number; there is no coercion annotation.
Filter, order and range structures use arbitrary serde_json::Value; documented nested shapes and numeric limits are not schema constraints. No local validation of GA field names or row limits.
offset is forwarded to the realtime API despite not being a RunRealtimeReportRequest field; supplying it may cause API rejection.

tools.name: create_custom_dimension
tools.description: Create a custom dimension on a GA4 property (registers an event parameter or user property so it can be used in reports). Requires the account to have edit rights and the `analytics.edit` OAuth scope. scope defaults to "EVENT"; parameter_name cannot be changed later.

property_id.description: GA4 property ID. Accepts: bare number (12345), string ("12345"), or resource name ("properties/12345")

parameter_name.description: The event parameter (or user property) name this dimension is registered against, e.g. "website_id", "suburb", "city". Max 24 chars for EVENT scope, 24 for USER scope. Cannot be changed after creation.

display_name.description: Human-readable display name shown in the GA UI, e.g. "Website ID".

scope.description: Scope of the dimension: "EVENT" (event parameter), "USER" (user property), or "ITEM" (ecommerce item parameter). Defaults to "EVENT".

description.description: Optional description of the custom dimension (max 150 chars).

disallow_ads_personalization.description: EVENT-scope only: if true, this dimension is NOT sent to Google signals / used for ads personalization. Optional.

tools.behavior: POST parameterName, displayName, scope (fallback EVENT), optional description and disallowAdsPersonalization. Property operations route through the cached Google account, or probe configured clients on cache miss; cached HTTP 403 clears the entry. API errors become MCP tool-error content.
notes: property_id is a JSON string despite description claiming acceptance of a bare number; there is no coercion annotation.
Documented enum choices, length limits and handler fallback defaults are prose/implementation only; no schemars enum, length, format or serde default constraints.

tools.name: create_property_annotation
tools.description: Create a reporting-data annotation on a GA4 property's timeline (e.g. to mark a deploy or campaign). Requires `analytics.edit`. Supply date as "YYYY-MM-DD"; add end_date for a date-range annotation.

property_id.description: GA4 property ID (bare number, string, or "properties/12345").

title.description: Annotation title, e.g. "Deployed bounding-box proximity search".

description.description: Optional longer description of what changed.

date.description: The date the annotation marks, as "YYYY-MM-DD". If end_date is also given, this is the start of a date-range annotation.

end_date.description: Optional end date "YYYY-MM-DD" to make this a date-range annotation instead of a single day.

color.description: Annotation color. One of: PURPLE, BROWN, BLUE, GREEN, RED, CYAN, ORANGE. Defaults to PURPLE. (The API rejects an unset color.)

tools.behavior: Parses date/end_date into integer year/month/day objects. POSTs title, color (fallback PURPLE), optional description and either annotationDate or annotationDateRange; local parsing errors return tool errors. Property operations route through the cached Google account, or probe configured clients on cache miss; cached HTTP 403 clears the entry. API errors become MCP tool-error content.
notes: property_id is a JSON string despite description claiming acceptance of a bare number; there is no coercion annotation.
Documented enum choices, length limits and handler fallback defaults are prose/implementation only; no schemars enum, length, format or serde default constraints.
Date parsing checks three integer components only; does not validate calendar ranges or date ordering.
Source review only; no tools/list, upstream execution or live requests. Git HEAD matches supplied revision.
All 15 tools register unconditionally through tool_router/tool_handler; write scope is required by Google APIs, not a local registration permission tier.

Schemars schemas reconstructed from JsonSchema/Deserialize models. No serde default/rename/flatten, enums or nested typed models occur. Option fields can be omitted or null; arbitrary Value schemas remain unconstrained. Additional properties are allowed by default.
Startup requires valid config credentials or ADC-discovered credentials before stdio serving. Runtime OAuth permissions and API enablement were not tested.
